articles.title: IAAPA Expo 2026 Sets Record with 39,000+ Attendees and 1,400 Exhibitors
articles.summary: IAAPA Expo 2026 was the largest in the event's history, drawing over 39,000 attendees and nearly 1,400 exhibiting companies across 634,000 square feet of exhibit space. The record-breaking show signals strong industry momentum and investment appetite heading into 2027. FEC operators and suppliers should take note of the growing supplier ecosystem and networking opportunities the event represents.

articles.title: 2026 IAAPA Brass Ring Award Winners Announced for Best Exhibit and Best New Product
articles.summary: The IAAPA Brass Ring Awards, among the industry's most prestigious honors, have named their 2026 winners for Best Exhibit and Best New Product. These awards highlight the most innovative suppliers and products entering the attractions market. FEC operators scouting new attractions and technology should pay close attention to this year's honorees.

articles.title: Triotech Unveils Five New Products at IAAPA Expo 2026 — Largest Release in Company History
articles.summary: Triotech debuted five new products at IAAPA Expo 2026, marking the largest single product launch in the company's history. The company is a key supplier of immersive media-based attractions frequently found in FECs, including dark rides and interactive experiences. Operators looking to refresh or expand their attraction mix should evaluate this new lineup.

articles.title: Zero Latency VR Launches Jumanji: The Lost Levels at Venues Worldwide
articles.summary: Zero Latency VR, the world's largest free-roam VR network, has opened bookings for Jumanji: The Lost Levels, available at its venues globally from December 4, 2026. The branded IP experience is designed for adventurers of all ages, broadening its demographic appeal. FEC operators hosting Zero Latency installations can expect renewed guest interest driven by the Jumanji franchise.

articles.title: Alterface Debuts Ultra-Low Latency Interactive Attraction Technology at IAAPA Expo 2026
articles.summary: Alterface showcased its newest interactive attraction system at IAAPA Expo 2026, featuring ultra-low latency of just 30 milliseconds and high-precision tracking for highly responsive guest interactions. The system also gives designers greater creative freedom in building interactive dark rides and shooting attractions. This technology is directly relevant to FEC operators investing in interactive and media-based attractions.

articles.title: Global Entertainment and Amusement Market Projected to Reach $96.9 Billion by 2033
articles.summary: A new Persistence Market Research report forecasts the global entertainment and amusement market will grow at a 4.8% CAGR to reach $96.9 billion by 2033. This sustained growth trajectory reflects strong consumer demand for out-of-home entertainment experiences. For FEC operators and investors, the data supports continued confidence in venue development and expansion strategies.

articles.title: Slick City Opens New 'Dry Waterpark' FEC in Schererville, Indiana
articles.summary: Slick City has opened a new family entertainment center in Schererville, Indiana, featuring its signature dry waterpark concept with slides, lanes, and active play attractions. The growing chain continues its national expansion, bringing its distinctive slide-based format to new Midwest markets. Competing FEC operators in the region should take note of the format's broad family appeal.

articles.title: Slick City Action Park Announces New Location in San Antonio
articles.summary: Slick City Action Park is continuing its rapid expansion with a new location planned for San Antonio, Texas, according to CoStar. The dry waterpark FEC format, which requires no water infrastructure, is proving highly scalable across diverse markets. San Antonio's addition underscores the brand's aggressive growth strategy and competitive pressure it places on existing local FECs.

articles.title: Slick City to Open New Boise Location on Milwaukee Street
articles.summary: Slick City is set to open yet another location in Boise, Idaho, further demonstrating the brand's rapid multi-market expansion across the U.S. The dry waterpark concept continues to gain traction as a differentiated FEC offering that appeals to families seeking active indoor entertainment. Local FEC operators should monitor this growing competitive presence.

articles.title: Level99 Expands to West Hartford with Life-Size Games and Competitive Social Attractions
articles.summary: Level99, the competitive socializing venue known for its life-size puzzle games and physical challenges, is opening a new location in West Hartford, Connecticut. The brand represents the growing trend of experience-based entertainment targeting adult and teen demographics beyond traditional FEC formats. Operators in the region and those tracking competitive socializing trends should follow this expansion closely.

articles.title: Elev8 Fun Overhauling Attractions at Seminole Towne Center Location
articles.summary: Elev8 Fun is undertaking a significant renovation of its Seminole Towne Center FEC, overhauling its attraction offerings to better serve guests. Attraction refreshes are increasingly critical for FECs competing with newer venues and evolving guest expectations. This move highlights the importance of regular reinvestment in attraction mix to maintain relevance and repeat visitation.

articles.title: EAG360 Announces Speaker Line-Up for January Industry Seminar Programme
articles.summary: EAG360, the co-located UK entertainment, attractions, and gaming trade event, has revealed its seminar speaker lineup for its upcoming January show, featuring leaders from hospitality, gaming, and attractions sectors. The programme includes 10 hours of content integrated directly into the show floor. FEC operators and suppliers with interests in the UK and European markets should consider attending.

articles.title: Good Stuff Launches B2B E-Commerce Platform to Streamline Ordering for Amusement Operators
articles.summary: Good Stuff has introduced a new B2B e-commerce platform designed specifically to simplify and speed up the ordering process for amusement and FEC customers. The platform aims to reduce friction in procurement, which is a persistent operational challenge for multi-location operators. FEC operators sourcing redemption merchandise and supplies should explore this new tool for potential efficiency gains.

articles.title: Red Raion Creating Power Rangers-Branded Media Content for 5D, VR, Dome, and Flying Theaters
articles.summary: Red Raion is developing media-based attraction content featuring Hasbro's Power Rangers IP, available across 5D, VR, dome, and flying theater formats. Branded IP content helps FEC operators attract new guest segments and drive repeat visits tied to recognizable entertainment properties. Operators running any of these theater formats should evaluate licensing this content.

articles.title: How Amusement Parks Are Rethinking Retail Placement to Meet Guest Needs
articles.summary: A new analysis explores how amusement parks and entertainment venues are repositioning retail to place products where guests naturally need them, rather than relying solely on traditional gift shop models. Strategic retail placement can meaningfully increase per-capita spending without significant capital investment. FEC operators looking to optimize ancillary revenue streams should review these insights.

articles.title: Xola Booking Platform Overview: Tools Built for Attractions and Escape Room Operators
articles.summary: Xola, founded in 2011, offers a comprehensive online booking and operations platform tailored to attractions operators including escape rooms, VR venues, and indoor experiences. The platform covers reservations, ticketing, payments, marketing, and OTA integrations in a single system. FEC operators evaluating or upgrading their reservation technology should consider Xola as a purpose-built solution for their sector.

articles.title: Brogent Partners with Major Entertainment Brands on New Flying Theater Attractions
articles.summary: Brogent Technologies has announced new partnerships with United Parks, Grupo Iter, Toho, and Sony to deliver flying theater attractions at venues worldwide. These collaborations expand Brogent's global footprint and bring high-profile IP to immersive flying ride formats. FEC operators and venue developers considering large-scale immersive attractions should follow Brogent's growing project pipeline.

articles.title: Texas FEC AR's Entertainment Hub Closes Abruptly After Nearly Six Years
articles.summary: AR's Entertainment Hub in Baytown, Texas shut its doors abruptly after nearly six years of operation, with little advance notice to customers. The closure is a cautionary example for FEC operators about the importance of financial planning, lease management, and transparent communication with guests. Industry stakeholders should examine the factors contributing to FEC closures in their own markets.

articles.title: UK's First Human Claw Machine Opens in Leicester, Highlighting Indoor Entertainment Innovation
articles.summary: Leicester has opened the UK's first human claw machine attraction, contributing to the city centre's growing reputation as an indoor entertainment hub. The novelty concept exemplifies the ongoing innovation in experiential entertainment formats that are driving foot traffic to FEC-style venues. Operators looking for differentiated, low-cost attraction ideas should take note of this emerging trend.

articles.title: New Multi-Activity Indoor Entertainment Venue Coming to Amble, UK
articles.summary: A new indoor entertainment venue offering a range of activities is set to open in Amble, Northumberland, expanding the FEC landscape in the UK's northeast. The development reflects continued demand for family-oriented indoor leisure in smaller and secondary markets. Suppliers and regional operators should monitor this growth in non-metropolitan FEC development.

articles.title: Omaha Property at 3002 Dodge Street May Be Converted into Indoor Entertainment Venue
articles.summary: A commercial property at 3002 Dodge Street in Omaha, Nebraska is being considered for conversion into an indoor entertainment venue, according to Hoodline. Repurposing underutilized retail or commercial real estate for FEC use is a growing trend, particularly in secondary markets. Developers and operators tracking site acquisition opportunities in the Midwest should follow this project.

articles.title: Rethinking Experience Design: Why Siloed Teams Are Holding Attractions Back
articles.summary: A thought leadership piece argues that the attractions and hospitality industries suffer when architecture, interiors, creative development, and engineering operate in isolated silos rather than collaborating across disciplines. The author makes the case for interdisciplinary design processes that prioritize overall guest experience over individual department performance. FEC owners and developers overseeing new builds or renovations should consider how their project structures may be limiting creative and operational outcomes.

articles.title: Four Lake Houston-Area Entertainment Venues Share Operational Updates
articles.summary: Four entertainment venues in the Lake Houston area have provided updates on their operations, offerings, and upcoming changes. Local venue news offers useful benchmarking for FEC operators tracking how competitors and peers are evolving their guest experience. Operators in the Houston metro and those following suburban FEC development should review these updates.

articles.title: Shooting Incident Near Baton Rouge Chuck E. Cheese Raises Safety Concerns for FEC Operators
articles.summary: A man was injured in a shooting near a Baton Rouge Chuck E. Cheese following an altercation that originated inside the venue. The incident underscores the ongoing safety and security challenges facing family entertainment centers, particularly those serving high-volume, mixed-demographic crowds. FEC operators should review their security protocols, staff training, and incident response procedures in light of events like this.

articles.title: Mississippi's 'The Gallery' Mixed-Use Development Wins TIF Approval, Includes FEC Component
articles.summary: Madison County, Mississippi has approved a TIF financing plan for 'The Gallery,' a mixed-use retail and dining development that includes an entertainment center component. Public financing tools like TIF are increasingly being used to support FEC-anchored developments in suburban markets. Operators and developers exploring public-private partnership structures should follow this project as a model.

articles.title: Querion Hypermedia Entertainment Park: A New Concept in Immersive Indoor Entertainment
articles.summary: Querion Hypermedia Entertainment Park is profiled as an emerging concept blending hypermedia technology with immersive entertainment in a park-style format. The concept represents a new frontier in technology-driven FEC design that could influence next-generation venue development. Operators and designers tracking innovation in immersive entertainment should explore this model.
